name: Telge Projects Ltd
title: Telge Projects Ltd - 544544 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Asset-light US-linked BIM/structural engineering firm reiterates 60–70% CAGR and ~35% EBITDA, but receivable days rose 73→108, supply side is headcount build, and no capacity or capex metrics were disclosed.

summary.headline: Telge Projects FY26 revenue rose about 57% to Rs 40.2 crore with Q4 EBITDA margin of 35%; order book stands at Rs 25 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue from operations of about Rs 40.2 crore (up about 57% from Rs 25.6 crore), with EBITDA of Rs 9.55 crore (24% margin) and PAT of Rs 5.9 crore (15% margin). Q4 revenue was Rs 14.4 crore (up 13.7% YoY, about 58% QoQ), with Q4 EBITDA of Rs 5 crore (35%) and PAT of Rs 3.3 crore (23%). Management said the current active order book is about Rs 25 crore, with a further Rs 6 crore in bidding, and guided to a 60-70% revenue CAGR and to maintaining Q4-level margins. Much of the answers were qualitative, and several figures were inconsistent or only partly answered.

segments.name: Standalone India (structural, BIM, steel and precast detailing)
segments.commentary: Standalone revenue grew about 22% YoY per the analyst's reading of the numbers, against about 60% consolidated growth. Management said the US subsidiaries handle sales and client relations while execution sits in the parent in India, so the entities cannot be cleanly separated.

segments.name: US subsidiaries (Midwest, Draftco, Edward Farr Architects)
segments.commentary: Edward Farr was acquired on 3 March and consolidated for about one month (about Rs 1.5 crore revenue, about Rs 40 lakh PAT). Edward Farr had CY2025 revenue of about Rs 14 crore and PAT margin of 10-12%, and was bought at 2.5x EBITDA. Management said about Rs 10 crore of the Rs 25 crore order book relates to the architecture business.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term revenue CAGR of 60-70%, with FY27 cited as the first year, though no absolute FY27 revenue figure was given.
Management aims to keep EBITDA and PAT margins at Q4 levels (EBITDA about 35%, PAT 20-23%) in FY27 and said it will not go below that.
Target project ticket size is Rs 8-10 crore, up from a previous highest of Rs 2-3 crore.
US billing rates are targeted at $45-60 per hour, up from $25-35 per hour previously.
Employee cost growth expected to slow in FY27 because no new leadership hires are planned; only execution-team expansion.
No debt plans; no equity raise planned 'not this year at least'.
About Rs 5 crore of IPO proceeds is earmarked for acquisitions, and several opportunities are under evaluation. MEP services are the stated next capability target.
capex_capacity: Nashik office became operational during FY26 and the Nashik team was expanded; Latur branch was added over the last 2-3 years.
Headcount is 200-250 in total, including about 25 in the US; about 70 people were added in FY26.
IPO proceeds: about Rs 7 crore utilised so far. Management said the office-premises object was deviated from, leaving Rs 5 crore for acquisitions.
demand_pricing: Order book is about Rs 25 crore (about 80% US), and a pipeline of about Rs 6 crore is at the RFQ or bidding stage, expected to convert within 2 weeks to a month.
Order book has been adding about Rs 4-5 crore per month over the last year, per management.
About 20 new clients were added in Q4, all from the US. Total customer count for FY26 was 96.
Management said the US-Iran conflict has had no impact on the business so far.
Seasonality: Q2 is the slowest quarter; Q4 is typically strongest.
Attrition in India is about 10% per management; subsidiary attrition is zero.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue reach 60-70% CAGR, and what is the go-to-market and visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the order book builds through the year and the Rs 6 crore RFQ pipeline is short-term. Cross-selling with Edward Farr and a higher ticket size (Rs 8-10 crore) are the longer-term drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY26 growth organic or inorganic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the acquisition closed on 3 March, so only one month was consolidated. Subsidiaries are now counted as organic growth, and inorganic growth will come from new acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivable days rise from 73 to 108?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most receivables are due in 30-45 days and that the major part of the balance is with a related party. Collections were accelerated in April and May, and DSO is now about 60 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why can EBITDA margin hold at 30-35% when peers run about 20-22%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited US-based teams that help secure higher billing rates ($45-60/hour target), expansion into lower-cost regions such as Nashik and Latur, and AI-led productivity gains.

qa_highlights.question: What is the share of recurring revenue and project duration?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing clients contribute 60-70% of revenue. Project duration varies from one month to a couple of years, and larger Rs 8-10 crore projects are expected to run longer.

qa_highlights.question: Is the employee cost increase sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 costs rose on deliberate leadership and business-development hires. No new leadership hires are planned for FY27, so growth in employee cost should be lower.

risks_watch: Receivable days rose sharply to 108 from 73. Management says DSO is now about 60, but the related-party share of receivables is material.
Organic growth is hard to separate from the US subsidiaries, which handle sales while India handles execution. Standalone growth was about 22%.
Full-year FY27 revenue of 60-70% growth implies about Rs 64-68 crore, which is not yet covered by the Rs 25 crore order book; the analyst questioned the visibility.
Employee cost is about 45% of revenue. The margin target depends on the bench being utilised.
Concentration: about 80% of the order book is US-based, so there is exposure to US infrastructure and macro conditions.
Acquisition pipeline and funding: Rs 5 crore earmarked for acquisitions, with no conclusion yet on identified targets.
AI-driven commoditisation of BIM modelling work could affect pricing; management did not give a specific response on this risk.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on long-term growth and margins, with a strong focus on the US expansion and AI. Evasive on several specifics: subsidiary-level margins, FY27 absolute revenue, and the current monthly run rate, which management declined to disclose. Answers on receivables and the consolidated versus standalone split were partial.
key_quotes: In the medium term, we are confident to achieve 60% to 70% CAGR growth in the upcoming financial year, that is FY2026-27, and relatively the next years as well.
So, for the next financial year, FY2026-27, we are trying to continue with the Q4 performance.
Now what we are targeting is $45 to $60 per hour even.
Yes, that is 100% going to expand and grow from what we have at the moment.

financial_highlights.metric: Employee cost as % of revenue (consolidated, per analyst)
financial_highlights.change: up from about 35% last year; not disputed by management

adds.what: Nashik office operational (became operational during FY26; team expanded)

growth.why: Management reiterated 60-70% revenue CAGR for FY27 with no absolute figure or bridge; backing is a ~Rs 25 crore active order book (about 80% US, adding Rs 4-5 crore per month) plus Rs 6 crore pipeline, ticket size and US billing-rate increases, but no specific capacity additions with numbers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management targets holding Q4 margins (EBITDA ~35%, PAT 20-23%) in FY27 versus FY26 full-year EBITDA of 24%, but employee cost rose to ~45% of revenue from ~35% and the bench-utilisation dependence is unproven.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Nashik office is already operational and Latur added over 2-3 years; no new plant, line or branch with numbers or dates was guided, and headcount is 200-250 with no new leadership hires planned.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management reiterated 60-70% revenue CAGR for FY27 (implying ~Rs 64-68 crore vs FY26 Rs 40.2 crore), backed by a ~Rs 25 crore active order book adding Rs 4-5 crore per month and a Rs 6 crore RFQ pipeline; no absolute FY27 figure or bridge was given, and the analyst questioned visibility.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed and no utilisation figure was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was held, not raised; the order book of ~Rs 25 crore covers only about 37-39% of the implied FY27 revenue range and management declined to give a monthly run rate.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The 60-70% CAGR implies ~Rs 64-68 crore against a Rs 25 crore order book, Q2 is seasonally the slowest quarter, and receivable days rose to 108 from 73 (management says ~60 now), with a material related-party share.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: MEP services is named as the next capability target and Rs 5 crore of IPO proceeds is earmarked for acquisitions, but no product launch date or detail was given.

rows.label: US billing rate increase to $45-60/hour
rows.why: Target is $45-60/hour versus $25-35 previously (about 1.5-2x), with the target ticket size of Rs 8-10 crore versus a prior high of Rs 2-3 crore, but no realised rate was disclosed.

rows.label: Debt-free and no equity raise
rows.why: Management stated no debt plans and no equity raise 'not this year at least', with the company funding growth from internal accruals and Rs 5 crore of IPO proceeds left for acquisitions.

rows.label: Receivable days normalisation to ~60
rows.why: DSO rose to 108 days from 73, management says it is now ~60 after April-May collections, but the related-party share of receivables is material and unverified.

tone.note: Management was confident on 60-70% CAGR, ~35% EBITDA margin and the US expansion, but evasive on subsidiary margins, FY27 absolute revenue and monthly run rate; analysts probed revenue visibility against the Rs 25 crore order book, the receivables jump and the standalone-vs-consolidated split.
